title: Automated model-retirement signals, pin warnings, and migration recipes
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Define and deliver an automated deprecation workflow that produces early retirement signals, targeted pin warnings, and publishable migration recipes for customers pinned to older model versions. This work enables low-friction migrations, reduces surprise outages when model variants are removed, and ties into Console, SDK warnings, and the onboarding checklist for new models.
background: We routinely surface new model variants and optimized weights. Customers frequently pin to specific versions for stability, which increases operational load during deprecation events. Current notices are manual: email blasts, static docs, and ad hoc SDK warnings. We need a deterministic, multi-channel deprecation workflow that triggers sensible defaults, provides migration guidance, and measures friction so the platform can automate safe rollouts and retirements.
scope:
- Instrument deprecation signal generation (age, usage, compatibility matrix, telemetry).
- Create Console UI components for deprecation timeline, pin detection, and migration recipes.
- Add SDK and API-level pin warnings and structured migration suggestions.
- Publish templated migration recipes and curated performance profile diffs.
- Provide admin controls for custodian teams to extend grace periods or pause notices.
out_of_scope:
- Automated customer data migrations (customers must opt-in to weight changes).
- Forced model replacements or automatic rewrites of pinned routes without explicit customer approval.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deprecation signal engine produces candidate lists with rationale (age, compatibility failures, critical bugs) and exposes an API.
- Console shows per-customer pinned routes with a deprecation badge and a 4-stage timeline (Notice, Warning, Pin-only grace, Retire).
- SDK logs a non-fatal warning when a pinned model has a scheduled retirement, including exact dates and link to migration recipe.
- Published migration recipes include: 1) compatibility matrix, 2) token-cost delta, 3) simple prompt/response example to validate parity.
- Metrics dashboard surfaces % pinned routes migrated and time-to-migrate.
- Documentation and customer-facing emails templates reviewed and approved by legal and CS.
rollout_plan:
1) Backend: signal engine and API (ENG) — feature-flagged internally.
2) Console: deprecation badges + per-route timeline (PM+Design+Eng) — behind permission toggle for accounts with >1 pinned route.
3) SDK: soft warning in minor release with link to Console; hard enforcement only after customer confirmation.
4) Docs & comms: publish migration recipes and email templates; run a small closed beta with 10 pilot customers.
5) Ramp: expand to all customers and enable automated weekly pin reports.
communication_plan:
- Week -8: Internal announcement to CS, Sales, Solutions with draft templates.
- Week -6: Open beta invite to customers with high pin density.
- Week -4: Official Notice (Console banner + email + SDK warning) with migration recipe link.
- Week -2: Pin-warning escalation (Console persistent banner per pinned route, in-API warning header).
- Retirement day: Final retire announcement, fallback routing enabled, post-mortem published.
engineering_tasks: ENG-5421: Build deprecation signal engine (age/usage/compatibility inputs) and REST API.
ENG-6080: Expose per-customer pin roster and route metadata used by Console and SDK.
ENG-6220: Implement SDK warning hook + telemetry for warning acknowledgement.
Add gates: feature flagging, rate-limited email sender, and A/B test hooks for messaging variants.
design_tasks: Create Console deprecation timeline component and pinned-route badge.
Design modal flow for migration recipe walkthrough and one-click migrate checklist (manual verification step).
Design email and in-console banner variants for A/B testing.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Customers miss emails or warnings -> Mitigation: Console-first persistent badges + SDK in-band warning.
Risk: False positives from the signal engine -> Mitigation: human-in-the-loop review for high-impact candidates and allow custodians to pause a retirement.
Risk: Migration causes quality regressions -> Mitigation: provide eval prompt sets, side-by-side sample outputs, and quick rollback guidance.
metrics: % of pinned routes with active retirement notices
Time-to-migrate (median, 90th percentile) from notice to migration
Migration success rate (parity validated by provided eval sets)
Number of support tickets referencing unexpected retirements
timeline:
Week 0-2: Signal engine and API prototype.
Week 3-5: Console components + SDK warning.
Week 6: Closed beta with pilot customers.
Week 7-8: Docs, templates, legal/CS review.
Week 9: Gradual public rollout and monitoring.
Week 12: Post-rollout review and health check.
notes:
- For early adopters, include a migration concierge option (CS-assisted) for enterprise accounts.
- Consider adding a telemetry tag that marks migrations done via our recipes to measure recipe effectiveness.
